Native libraries (AWS-LC, SQLite bundled, libxml2/xmlsec) are covered by cargo deny/RustSec and the image scan (docs/security/supply-chain.md).

OpenTrack ships as one immutable container image (Dockerfile) with a read-only root filesystem, so an upgrade replaces the whole application and no older OpenTrack files remain inside the running container (docs/guides/admin.md#upgrades). Removing superseded images and old binaries from hosts/registries is the site's task.
comments: Site: host / container platform administrator (prune superseded images).

finding_details: The project checks dependencies continuously in CI (cargo deny RustSec advisories, npm audit; .github/workflows/ci.yml) and documents rebuilding on Debian security updates (docs/security/hardening.md#operate, docs/security/supply-chain.md); the release image scan is produced with scripts/ato/scan. Checking IAVMs/CTOs weekly and applying updates is the operating site's patch process.
comments: Site: ISSO / system administrator patch process (IAVM/CTO tracking).

finding_details: OpenTrack verifies its security functions: at start fips::init enables AWS-LC in FIPS mode, which runs the module's power-on self-tests, and refuses to run if they or the FIPS TLS provider fail (crates/ot-server/src/fips.rs, docs/security/fips.md#what-the-process-checks); SAML is refused unless OpenSSL reports FIPS mode (auth/saml.rs); client-certificate CRL checks fail closed (https.rs); the audit hash chain is verified on demand (GET /api/v1/audit/verify, crates/ot-server/src/audit_api.rs) and its head logged hourly (auth/maintenance.rs).

Verification runs at every start/restart (FIPS power-on self-tests and FIPS provider check in crates/ot-server/src/fips.rs init; process exits on failure) and upon command by a privileged user (admin-only GET /api/v1/audit/verify checks the whole audit hash chain and records the result as an audit_verify event, crates/ot-server/src/audit_api.rs verify).

On failure OpenTrack emits the evidence: a failed FIPS self-test stops the process with an error; a broken audit chain logs an ERROR ("the audit record's hash chain is broken") and writes an audit_verify failure row, which is exported as an audit.record OTLP log event (crates/ot-server/src/audit_api.rs, telemetry.rs, docs/guides/admin.md#audit-record). OpenTrack has no direct notification channel (no email by design); alerting the ISSO/ISSM on these events is done by the site's SIEM/collector.
comments: Site: SIEM alert rules routing these events to the ISSO/ISSM.

finding_details: The only mobile code is the React single-page application's JavaScript, which executes within the client browser; per the check text this makes the rule not applicable. No ActiveX, Java applets or other Category 1A mobile code is shipped (ui/, CSP script-src 'self' in crates/ot-server/src/control.rs).

Account management process and prompt removal of departed users are ISSO duties. OpenTrack supports them: Settings -> Users and opentrack user CLI to create/disable/remove accounts, automatic disable after 35 days of inactivity, API-token revocation on disable, and every change audited (docs/guides/admin.md#users, docs/security/stig-mapping.md AC-2, AC-2(3)).
comments: Site: ISSO account management process.

finding_details: Network placement (DoD DMZ tiering) is decided by the hosting site. OpenTrack's roles (serve, sources, engine, writer, cot) can run as separate processes/containers, and SQLite/Redis/NATS are separate services, so tiers can be separated (README.md#architecture, docs/guides/admin.md#server-roles).
comments: Site: network architecture / DMZ owner.

finding_details: OpenTrack keeps its local audit table forever (append-only, nothing deletes rows; docs/guides/admin.md#audit-record, crates/ot-store/src/audit.rs) and exports every record over OTLP to the site's collector/SIEM. Retaining 30 months (5 years for SAMI) in active and cold storage is the site's retention process.
comments: Site: ISSO / SIEM retention policy.

finding_details: Periodic audit review is an ISSO process. OpenTrack provides the record in the SIEM (audit.record OTLP events), GET /api/v1/audit with filters and CSV for admins, and chain verification (docs/guides/admin.md#audit-record, docs/security/hardening.md#operate says to review at the interval the plan sets).
comments: Site: ISSO audit review procedure and records.

finding_details: Reporting suspected IA violations is an organisational SOP; OpenTrack supplies the events (failed sign-ins, lockouts, refused SAML, broken chain) in its audit record and logs.
comments: Site: ISSO incident reporting SOP.

finding_details: Active vulnerability and fuzz testing of the deployed application is the ISSO's responsibility. The project provides CI dependency scanning (cargo deny, npm audit; .github/workflows/ci.yml) and an image scanner script (scripts/ato/scan), but no DAST or fuzzing results are shipped.
comments: Site: ISSO-directed DAST/fuzz testing and scan results.

finding_details: The design is documented as a one-directional pipeline (feeds -> sources -> Redis streams -> engine -> outbox -> writer/cot) with an execution-flow diagram (README.md#architecture); the API reaches the engine only through a Redis command queue and waits with a timeout (logged as 'the engine did not answer'), so no service calls back into its caller. Loops between nodes are prevented by design: OpenTrack ignores its own messages and reports carry only the sender's sources (docs/sync-icd.md, docs/multi-node.md echo tests).

Application code and control/configuration files live in the read-only image (/usr/local/bin/opentrack, /opt/opentrack/ui, /opt/opentrack/profiles, /etc/opentrack/*.cnf; Dockerfile, read_only: true in docker-compose.yml); runtime settings come from environment variables. Writable state is only the /data volume (database, session.key, imported profiles; docs/guides/admin.md#data-directory), owned by the non-root opentrack user; application users have no file-system access, only the role-checked API. The signing key can instead come from OT_SESSION_SECRET via the site's secret store.

Configuring third-party components (Redis, NATS, host OS, container runtime, reverse proxy) per available guidance is the site's task. OpenTrack's docs give the settings it depends on: TLS/mTLS for Redis and NATS, Redis tls-auth-clients, container hardening (docs/security/hardening.md#encrypt-every-link, #before-first-start).
comments: Site: ISSO / system administrator.

finding_details: PPSM registration of IPs, ports and services is a site/program action. OpenTrack's listening and outbound ports are configurable and documented in scattered places (OT_BIND default 8090, TAK outputs 8087/8089 and SA multicast, source listeners such as UDP/gRPC binds, NATS, Redis, OTLP 4317/4318; docs/guides/admin.md, docs/security/hardening.md); the package has no single ports/protocols list.
comments: Site: ISSO submits the PPS list to DoD PPSM.

finding_details: Registration in the DoD Ports and Protocols Database is done for a production site by its program/ISSO, using the ports the site configures (see V-222628).
comments: Site: ISSO / program office.

finding_details: The CM repository is hosted on GitHub (private repository; .github/workflows/). Its patching and STIG compliance are the responsibility of the developer organisation / hosting provider and cannot be verified from the code.
comments: Developer organisation: CM repository owner.

finding_details: Quarterly review of CM repository access is a developer-organisation process; the repository documents branch protection (scripts/github/protect-main.sh) but no access review records.
comments: Developer organisation: CM administrator (quarterly access review).

finding_details: docs/security/scm-plan.md is the software configuration management plan: the configuration items (source, lockfiles, pinned toolchain in rust-toolchain.toml, base images by digest, checksummed build inputs, forks in third_party/ with their OPENTRACK.md notes, the vendored stareSDK in ui/vendor, deny.toml, workflows, signing key, accreditation sources) and the released artefacts; the repository and branch rules (main protected by scripts/github/protect-main.sh, with the admin bypass and the current single-maintainer practice stated); version identification and CHANGELOG.md; the release process (tag, signed image with provenance and SBOMs, scan, coverage summary, GitHub pre-release); change control through issues and pull requests; configuration of deployed nodes (config export/import); and roles.
comments: The organisational CCB (V-222633) remains the site's.

finding_details: A Configuration Control Board is an organisational body; its charter and meeting records cannot be verified from the repository.
comments: Developer organisation / program office: CCB charter and minutes.

finding_details: IPv6 is supported throughout: listeners and clients bind and connect over IPv6, UDP sources join IPv6 multicast groups (interface by name or index) and the TAK multicast output sends to IPv6 groups (crates/ot-source/src/transport.rs, crates/ot-server/src/cot/output.rs; tests udp_joins_an_ipv6_multicast_group, sends_multicast_sa_over_ipv6).
Whether the host is dedicated for a mission-critical application is a hosting decision; OpenTrack runs as its own container (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml).
comments: Site: ISSO / hosting.

finding_details: The contingency plan is the site's. OpenTrack documents what to back up, how to restore and how to rebuild a node from a configuration export (docs/guides/admin.md#backup-and-restore, #rebuild-a-node-from-a-configuration-export) and supports several nodes sharing one picture (docs/multi-node.md).
comments: Site: contingency plan owner.

finding_details: The disaster recovery plan is the site's. OpenTrack provides recovery features: documented restore (docs/guides/admin.md#restore), PRAGMA integrity_check for backups, migrations that refuse a newer schema, audit hash-chain verification after restore (GET /api/v1/audit/verify), and FIPS self-tests on restart.
comments: Site: DR plan including trusted recovery steps.

finding_details: Performing backups at the required interval is a site process. OpenTrack documents online SQLite backup (sqlite3 .backup / VACUUM INTO), Redis backup, session.key and configuration export (docs/guides/admin.md#backup-and-restore).
comments: Site: system administrator backup schedule and off-site storage.

finding_details: Off-site or fire-rated storage of software and source copies is organisational. Source is held in a hosted Git repository and releases are published as signed images to ghcr.io (docs/security/supply-chain.md#releases); the site must keep its own copy of the deployed image.
comments: Site / developer organisation: off-site software backups.

finding_details: Physical and technical protection of backup and restoration assets is a site procedure; the admin guide warns that the database, session.key, .env and configuration exports hold secrets and must be kept safe (docs/guides/admin.md#what-to-back-up), and stig-mapping.md SC-28 leaves volume/backup encryption to the platform.
comments: Site: backup and recovery procedures.

finding_details: All key exchange is done by TLS 1.2/1.3 through rustls' FIPS configuration on the AWS-LC FIPS 140-3 module (ECDHE on NIST curves, AES-GCM), with server certificates validated and mutual TLS available on the UI/API, NATS, Redis, feeds and OTLP (crates/ot-server/src/fips.rs init, crates/ot-server/src/https.rs, crates/ot-source/src/tls.rs, docs/security/fips.md, docs/security/hardening.md#encrypt-every-link).

No credentials, keys or certificates are embedded in code or configuration: the repository has no private keys or credential files (only cosign.pub), secrets come from environment variables or ${env:...} references (docs/examples/aisstream.json, docker-compose.yml with empty defaults), the session key is generated at first start into /data/session.key with owner-only permissions, and the only literal passwords are in #[cfg(test)] tests (e.g. crates/ot-server/src/auth/api.rs tests).

Each labelled track has one portion marking (ot-core SecurityLabel::marking, e.g. (S//REL TO USA, GBR)): TAK/CoT events carry a <detail><__security .../> element and remarks starting with the marking; track exports (GeoJSON, CSV), the audit CSV, registry sheets and the configuration export are marked (crates/ot-server/src/marking.rs); the UI shows each track's marking; NATS carries the label. Tests: markings_follow_us_syntax, a_labelled_track_carries_its_marking, a_file_is_marked_by_its_highest_label_else_the_banner.

Every change runs the test suites before merge: cargo fmt/clippy -D warnings/cargo test (with Redis, NATS and MQTT services) and UI lint/test/build, required as status checks on main (.github/workflows/ci.yml, scripts/github/protect-main.sh); README.md#tests describes the tests and scripts/check.sh the end-to-end check; each release's changes and upgrade steps are in CHANGELOG.md.

Release images are identified by SHA-256 digest, signed with the project's cosign key, verified in the release workflow, and the digest is attached to the release (image-digest.txt) with SBOMs and SLSA provenance (.github/workflows/release.yml); the documented deployment step is to verify the signature by digest before running (docs/security/hardening.md#before-first-start, docs/security/supply-chain.md#releases).
Designating a security tester is an organisational staffing decision that cannot be verified from the repository.
comments: Developer organisation: named security tester.

finding_details: Annual test procedures and dates are a site/developer process. OpenTrack's secure-state behaviour on initialisation and abort is built in (process stops if FIPS self-tests fail, fips.rs; sign-in fails closed if it can't be audited; every /api/v1 route checks the session and role, auth/policy.rs), but no annual test procedure document ships.
comments: Site / developer organisation: annual secure-state test procedure and records.

finding_details: Code review is a developer-organisation process. The repository shows a PR workflow requiring one approval and passing CI before merge (scripts/github/protect-main.sh, merge commits such as 'Merge pull request #55'), clippy -D warnings and unsafe_code forbidden, but branch protection lets admins bypass and no code review reports covering the listed flaw classes are in the package.
comments: Developer organisation: provide code review records / SAST report per release.

finding_details: scripts/coverage.sh measures test coverage of the Rust workspace with cargo-llvm-cov, running the tests against real Redis, NATS and MQTT, and writes target/coverage/summary.txt. docs/security/scm-plan.md#releases makes attaching the coverage summary to each GitHub release part of the release process and records the figures at the start of the practice. The UI's Vitest suite runs without a coverage figure (no coverage provider is a UI dependency); the script measures it where one is installed.
comments: Coverage is recorded per release, not gated.

finding_details: Flaws are tracked in the project's GitHub issue tracker and carried into the security documentation: findings F-1..F-9 with their status (docs/security/stig-mapping.md#findings) and issue numbers referenced in CHANGELOG.md (e.g. #50, #53).

IA and accreditation impact assessment of changes is a CCB/ISSO process. The project flags security-relevant changes in CHANGELOG.md and docs (e.g. docs/security/fips.md: an aws-lc-fips-sys change is a crypto change; supply-chain.md: moving base images), but the assessment itself is organisational.
comments: Developer organisation / ISSO: CCB impact assessment records.

finding_details: Security flaws are fixed or carried in the plan: stig-mapping.md#findings lists F-1..F-9 with fixed/accepted/open status (F-5 inline styles open, low; F-4 accepted), missing OCSP is on the roadmap (#21), and fixes are recorded in CHANGELOG.md.

docs/security/coding-standards.md is the coding standard: the rules the tools enforce in CI and scripts/check.sh (rustfmt, clippy -D warnings on all targets, unsafe_code = forbid for every crate, dbg_macro, --locked builds, the pinned toolchain, cargo-deny and npm audit, the UI type check, oxlint and tests) and the rules checked in review: FIPS-only cryptography through aws-lc-rs and the rustls FIPS provider, secrets handling (ot_core::secrets, ${env:NAME}, nothing secret in logs or audit), errors (ApiError::internal answers with a reference), input limits and validation, roles for new routes, UI rules (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, CSP), the dependency policy and test expectations.

Design documentation is maintained with each release: architecture and data flow (README.md#architecture), external interfaces and exchanged data (docs/nats-output.md, docs/sync-icd.md, docs/protobuf-grpc.md, docs/non-point-contacts.md, admin guide TAK output), protections on each interface (docs/security/hardening.md#encrypt-every-link), roles and privileges (docs/guides/admin.md#roles, auth/policy.rs), security requirements and sensitive data handling (docs/security/stig-mapping.md, fips.md, admin.md#security-labels), updated per release in CHANGELOG.md.

docs/security/threat-model.md is the threat model: a data-flow diagram and trust boundaries, then STRIDE threats, current mitigations (citing code and documents), residual risk and the POA&M item for each interface (UI/API, SAML, client certificates and OpenStare sign-in, source transports, plugins, Redis, NATS, multi-node sync, TAK, OpenTelemetry, SQLite and the data volume, the image and supply chain), and a criticality analysis. It is re-reviewed for every minor release and with any change that adds an interface or trust boundary.

Errors are handled without leaking internals: 5xx answers are generic with a reference and logged in full (control.rs), sign-in refusals are uniform, and Rust's typed errors mean no unhandled exception reaches the client; tested in control.rs.

SECURITY.md is the product's vulnerability and incident response process: how to report (privately to the maintainer on GitHub; sites through their own channel), acknowledgement within 5 working days, confirmation and severity within 10, fix or mitigation targets by severity (Critical/High 30 days), private tracking until the fix ships and then an issue labelled security, the fix with a regression test and the accreditation documents updated in the same pull request, and notification of users through release notes, CHANGELOG Security fixes and advisories.
comments: The site's own incident response plan (IR-8) covers the deployment.

finding_details: Support is contractual/organisational. OpenTrack is developed and released by its development team (CHANGELOG.md, releases), labelled alpha (docs/guides/admin.md#upgrades); its base OS is Debian bookworm and dependencies are pinned and scanned (docs/security/supply-chain.md). Proof of a support agreement must come from the program.
comments: Program office / site: support agreement with the development team.

finding_details: Decommissioning when support ends is a program/site decision.
comments: Program office / ISSO.

finding_details: Notifying users of decommissioning is an organisational procedure; OpenTrack's notice-and-consent and classification banners (Settings -> Banners) could carry such a notice.
comments: Site: ISSO / program communications procedure.

finding_details: OpenTrack has no vendor or built-in accounts. Only when the database has no accounts does serve create a first admin, from OT_ADMIN_EMAIL/OT_ADMIN_PASSWORD (checked against the password policy) or admin@opentrack.local with a random generated password written owner-only to initial-admin.txt and flagged must-change (crates/ot-server/src/auth/mod.rs bootstrap_admin; docs/guides/admin.md#first-admin). No service or guest accounts exist.

There is no published default password: the first admin's password is either the operator's policy-checked OT_ADMIN_PASSWORD or a random one generated by the FIPS DRBG and marked temporary so the first sign-in forces a change (crates/ot-server/src/auth/mod.rs bootstrap_admin, auth/password.rs generate). Note: docs/guides/admin.md#first-admin still says 'at least 8 characters', while the code enforces the full policy.

The administrator guide and hardening checklist are the configuration guide: encryption and PKI (docs/guides/admin.md#tls, #client-certificates, docs/security/fips.md), password/lockout/session settings (#password-policy etc.), audit (#audit-record, #opentelemetry), SAML/IdP (#saml), backup and recovery (#backup-and-restore), network links (docs/security/hardening.md#encrypt-every-link), deployment (#installation, docker-compose.yml) and security assumptions (docs/security/stig-mapping.md inherited controls).

Whether the deployment processes classified data, and its Security Classification Guide, are determined by the program/data owner. OpenTrack carries per-source classification labels but defines no classified data elements itself (docs/guides/admin.md#security-labels).
comments: Program office / data owner: SCG covering the track data.

finding_details: The only mobile code is the SPA's JavaScript bundle served from the same origin under a CSP with script-src 'self' and no inline script (crates/ot-server/src/control.rs; F-5 concerns inline styles only). The UI ships no WebAssembly, Flash, Java or ActiveX; WebAssembly plugins run on the server, not in the browser.

Whether production data is exported to test/development is a site practice. OpenTrack's configuration export includes secrets and the admin guide says to keep it as safe as the database (docs/guides/admin.md#configuration-export); non-admin API views mask source credentials (F-2).
comments: Site: data owner / system administrator sanitisation procedure.

finding_details: Application-level DoS protections are implemented: per-address sign-in rate limit and account lockout (crates/ot-server/src/auth/mod.rs allow_attempt), request body limits (axum default 2 MB, DefaultBodyLimit on import routes), bounded Redis streams and outbox (MAXLEN/MINID, OT_OBS_WINDOW_SECS), per-track output throttling, timeouts on plugin calls and dependency checks, and WASM plugin resource grants (crates/ot-plugin/src/grants.rs). Network-level DoS protection is the site's.

OpenTrack reports resources (CPU, memory, threads, Redis memory, SQLite and NATS stream size, backlogs) on the Overview, /api/v1/metrics and as OTLP metrics, and dependency failures via /api/v1/status (503) (docs/guides/admin.md#monitoring, crates/ot-server/src/metrics.rs), but it does not itself raise a low-disk or low-memory alert; alert thresholds are set in the site's monitoring/SIEM.
comments: Site / platform: monitoring alert rules on OpenTrack metrics and host resources.

finding_details: Registering an administrator for update and security notifications is a site action.
comments: Site: system administrator subscription to release/advisory notifications.

finding_details: SECURITY.md (How fixes are announced) defines the security notification process: every fix is published in the GitHub release notes and CHANGELOG.md under Security fixes, and each Medium or higher gets an advisory giving the description, affected versions, severity, fixed version, how to obtain the signed image, and interim mitigations: a GitHub Security Advisory once the repository is public (GitHub offers them only then), a Security advisory section of the release notes until then. Supported versions are stated (latest 0.4.x). The 0.4.3 release notes already carry a Security fixes section.
comments: Users are notified by watching the repository's releases; the application does not check for updates itself.

finding_details: Whether OpenTrack is reachable from the Internet and routed through a DMZ is a site network decision.
comments: Site: network / boundary owner.

finding_details: Every sign-in writes a login audit row with the client address and session id (crates/ot-server/src/auth/api.rs start_session: AuditEvent login .ip), so a second, concurrent sign-in from another workstation records its own IP; sessions beyond the limit of 3 are ended and audited as session ended with reason limit and their address. Rows are also exported as audit.record events (docs/guides/admin.md#audit-record).
Annual security training of the program's managers, designers, developers and testers is an organisational record that cannot be verified from the repository.
comments: Developer organisation / program manager: training records.

finding_details: Whether the deployment processes classified data, and the required NSA-approved protection, is determined by the AO/data owner. OpenTrack uses only FIPS 140-3 validated modules (AWS-LC FIPS, OpenSSL 3.0.9 FIPS provider; docs/security/fips.md) with TLS for every link; it has no Type 1 or CSfC capability of its own, and data at rest encryption is left to the platform (stig-mapping.md SC-28).
comments: Site / AO: classified-data encryption (Type 1/CSfC network and storage encryption) if classified data is processed.
